To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dialecticism, a cognitive orientation to tolerate contradictions, was associated with ingroup disfavor in Chinese but not in Latinos and European Americans.
dialecticism is associated with ingroup disfavor in East Asian cultures, and this association is mediated by lay beliefs.
dialecticism, a lay belief that is more prevalent in East Asia, is negatively associated with positive ingroup attitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dialecticism in shaping ingroup favoritisms, and it is the first to demonstrate a link between dialecticism and in group derogation.
the role that cultural differences play in shaping ingroup attitudes and how these cultural differences may be reflected at the explicit versus implicit levels.
how cultural beliefs influence the way people think and feel about their ingroups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dialecticism is associated with negative ingroup attitudes.

dialectical lay beliefs may be associated with negative ingroup attitudes among East Asians, whereas such beliefs may be associated more with positive ingroup attitudes among North Americans (see the article for details).
dialecticism is associated with ingroup derogation, but only when the ingroup is defined as a family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cultural differences in ingroups are more complex than previously thought.
the dialecticism hypothesis can account for the cultural differences in ingrouf favoritism.
dialectical thinking may be an important factor in explaining cultural differences in ingroups and outgroups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cultural differences in lay beliefs may have important implications for understanding cultural differences in ingroups favoritism.
dialecticism, a cognitive tendency that is more frequently found in East Asian than in European American cultures, can explain the cultural differences in ingroups attitudes.
dialectical lay beliefs may be an important moderator of the expression of ingroup attitudes, which may explain cultural differences in the expression of ingroupprejudice.
